links.comparator_used: First readers (breast radiologists) in a double-read screening programme, compared with standalone AI replacing the first reader at two cut-offs
links.outcome: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, recall rate, and screen-detected versus interval cancers detected
links.effect: AI_spec was comparable to first readers on all accuracy measures. AI_sens had lower specificity (97.5% vs 97.7%; p < 0.0001) and PPV (17.5% vs 18.7%; p = 0.01) and a higher recall rate (3.0% vs 2.8%; p < 0.0001). Both AI settings detected fewer screen-detected cancers (1166 AI_sens, 1156 AI_spec vs 1252; p < 0.0001) but more interval cancers (126 AI_sens, 117 AI_spec vs 39; p < 0.0001).
links.tradeoff: AI and first readers detected a different mix of cancers, with AI missing more screen-detected cancers. Matching at sensitivity gave a higher recall rate and lower PPV.
links.quote: AI<sub>spec</sub> was comparable to first readers in terms of all accuracy measures.

design_hint: alert threshold selection (AI cut-off matched to reader sensitivity or specificity)
